name: Question 10
problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $C$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9{R}_{1}
$$

Given that $C$ has the LU factorization $C=LU,$ then $L=$
worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+9\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $C$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot C=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}C=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}C & =U \\ {E}_{1}C & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ C & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ C & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ C & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 \\ -9 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

Applying R2:=R2+1⋅R1 and then R3:=R3+9⋅R1 is equivalent to multiplying C from the left by the following elementary matrices:

[100010901]⏟E2⋅[100110001]⏟E1⋅C=U

Now, since E2E1C=U, we can invert E2 and E1 to arrive at the desired LU factorization: E2E1C=UE1C=E2−1UC=E1−1E2−1UC=[100110001]−1[100010901]−1UC=([100−110001][100010−901])UC=[100−110−901]⏟L⋅U
